description: Player (vsmp.py) side of the image queue: a shared ffmpeg scale/pad(white)/gray filter helper factored out of extract_frame(), queue configuration and helpers (list/claim/dispose/startup-sweep), the top-of-tick queue check in play_movie() that displays a queued image for one tick WITHOUT advancing state['frame'] while still pinging the watchdog and respecting sleep_until(next_deadline), and an images_shown counter in state + summarize_state + CLI status. Plus stub-based tests proving the queue-drain contract. This feature is the foundation FEAT-002 depends on (it exposes the conversion helper and fixes QUEUE_DIR / the queue-dir layout). It leaves the suite green on its own.
steps: In vsmp.py, factor the video filter out of extract_frame(): add a helper panel_video_filter(geometry) returning the string 'scale={w}:{h},pad=800:480:{px}:{py}:color={color},format=gray' built from a geometry dict, and have extract_frame() call it so its behaviour is unchanged. This is a behaviour-preserving refactor.

Add convert_image_to_panel_png(src_path, out_path) to vsmp.py: ffprobe the source image's own width/height, build geometry via panel_geometry(width, height, sar=Fraction(1), bar_color='white') (SAR 1:1, white letterbox per design doc section 4), run ONE ffmpeg pass (via run_tool with FFMPEG_TIMEOUT_S) using panel_video_filter() to write an 800x480 grayscale PNG, and raise a clear error if the output is missing or zero bytes ('ffmpeg produced a non-empty PNG'). This function must be importable by webapp.py and must NOT import the epd driver. Reuse run_tool/probe conventions already in the file.

Add queue config: a module constant QUEUE_DIR defaulting to 'queue' (overridable via env VSMP_QUEUE), and a --queue-dir option on the 'play' subparser in parse_args(), plumbed exactly like --state (default QUEUE_DIR). Thread the resolved queue dir into cmd_play() and play_movie().

Add queue helpers to vsmp.py. queue_paths(queue_dir) -> returns (queue_dir, incoming_dir, showing_dir) as Paths for <queue>/, <queue>/.incoming/, <queue>/.showing/ and mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) them. list_queue(queue_dir) -> sorted list of Path for queue_dir/*.png ONLY (never .incoming or .showing; because they are dotfile subdirs, a plain glob('*.png') already excludes them). claim_next_image(queue_dir) -> pick the lexically smallest published *.png, os.rename it into .showing/ with the same name, return the new path, or None if the queue is empty; tolerate a FileNotFoundError race (another consumer won it) by retrying the next candidate or returning None. dispose_shown_image(path) -> by default unlink it; if env VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR is set, move it there instead and prune the archive to the most-recent VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX files (default 50) by sorted name, so the archive is always capped. sweep_showing(queue_dir) -> delete any leftover files under .showing/ (a claimed file was already taken and must never be re-shown), mirroring clean_frame_dir(); log how many were removed.

Modify play_movie(): call sweep_showing(queue_dir) once near the top beside clean_frame_dir(). At the TOP of the while loop, before render_one_frame, call claim_next_image(queue_dir). If it returns a path: load it with prepare_for_panel(path, contrast), display via display_on_e_ink(epd, image), dispose_shown_image(path), increment state['images_shown'], advance next_deadline by FRAME_INTERVAL_S (with the same behind-schedule re-anchoring the movie path uses), update state['next_frame_local'], call save_state(), emit a structured log line tagged as an image tick (e.g. 'image=<name> images_shown=N next=...'), call watchdog_ping(), then sleep_until(next_deadline) and continue the loop WITHOUT incrementing state['frame'] and WITHOUT touching any movie frame field (timecode/percent/last_extract_s/etc). If it returns None, the existing movie-frame path runs unchanged. Ensure images are still serviced when the movie is finished or at end-of-movie: restructure the loop so the queue check runs each tick regardless of state['frame'] vs total (e.g. loop while there is movie left OR the queue is non-empty), so uploads keep displaying after the film ends; keep the existing 'finished movie, nothing to do' early-return in cmd_play unchanged for the no-queue case, or document precisely which behaviour was chosen in the FEAT findings.

Add images_shown to state and surface it: add 'images_shown': 0 to new_state(); load_state() already setdefault()s new keys so older files stay valid; add images_shown to summarize_state() output and print it in cmd_status().

Add tests/test_queue.py following tests/test_state_loop.py conventions (import harness BEFORE vsmp; use FakeEpd; set vsmp.FRAME_INTERVAL_S small). Build 800x480 self-identifying gray PNGs (a distinct solid gray per image, like make_fixtures.py) and drop them into the queue dir under test. Assert: the queue drains one image per tick in FIFO (lexical-name) order verified by reading a pixel; state['frame'] does NOT advance on an image tick; the movie resumes at the exact next frame after the queue empties; images_shown increments once per image; the shown file is deleted by default and .showing/ is empty afterwards; sweep_showing() removes a pre-seeded leftover .showing/ file at startup; an image dropped into the queue mid-tick is NOT shown until the following tick (no mid-tick swap). Add a NEGATIVE CONTROL: with an empty queue the movie advances normally (state['frame'] increments, images_shown stays 0). Add tests/test_queue to the MODULES list in tests/run.py.
Run the suite and clean up any stray files so the repo-cleanliness assertions in test_state_loop pass.
acceptance_criteria: extract_frame() still produces correct frames: `python3 tests/run.py test_extract test_state_loop` passes with no regressions.

`python3 tests/run.py test_queue` passes all new assertions: one image per tick, FIFO order, frame counter unchanged on image ticks, movie resumes, images_shown increments, disposal (delete default) happens, .showing/ sweep works, no mid-tick swap, and the empty-queue NEGATIVE CONTROL.
vsmp.convert_image_to_panel_png() produces an output readable by PIL as exactly 800x480 that passes display_on_e_ink()'s size guard, and raises on a non-image input.
vsmp.py still never imports the epd driver at module top; convert_image_to_panel_png and the queue helpers are importable without the driver.
The full suite `python3 tests/run.py` stays green (only the optional real-movie checks skipped) and the repo is left clean.
verification: python3 -c "import vsmp, PIL.Image as I; from pathlib import Path; p=I.new('RGB',(1234,987),(200,30,30)); p.save('/tmp/feat1_in.png'); vsmp.convert_image_to_panel_png('/tmp/feat1_in.png','/tmp/feat1_out.png'); o=I.open('/tmp/feat1_out.png'); print('size', o.size, 'mode', o.mode); assert o.size==(800,480)"
findings:
Implemented in vsmp.py; full suite green (214 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped optional real-movie checks) and all three FEAT-001 verification commands pass. Contracts FEAT-002 (webapp) depends on:

CONVERSION HELPER: vsmp.convert_image_to_panel_png(src_path, out_path) -- final name, exactly as specced. Takes str-or-Path for both args, returns the output Path. ffprobes the source's own width/height, builds geometry via panel_geometry(w, h, sar=Fraction(1), bar_color='white') (SAR 1:1, WHITE letterbox), then runs ONE ffmpeg pass using the new shared helper panel_video_filter(geometry) to write an 800x480 grayscale (PIL mode 'L') PNG. Raises RuntimeError on a non-image/empty-output ('ffmpeg produced a non-empty PNG...'). Driver-free: webapp.py can `import vsmp` and call it without ever importing the epd driver (confirmed: importing vsmp pulls in no epd module). Output passes display_on_e_ink()'s exact-800x480 size guard. The webapp must do its own atomic write-then-rename: convert into <queue>/.incoming/<name>.tmp then os.rename into <queue>/<name>.png.

SHARED FILTER: panel_video_filter(geometry) -> 'scale={w}:{h},pad=800:480:{px}:{py}:color={color},format=gray' built from a panel_geometry() dict (keys width,height,pad_x,pad_y,pad_color). extract_frame() now calls it too (behaviour-preserving refactor, verified by test_extract).

QUEUE_DIR: module constant QUEUE_DIR = os.environ.get('VSMP_QUEUE', 'queue'). The play subparser has --queue-dir (default QUEUE_DIR), plumbed through cmd_play -> play_movie(..., queue_dir=...). webapp.py should read the SAME dir from VSMP_QUEUE so player and web server agree.

LAYOUT + FIFO CONTRACT: queue_paths(queue_dir) returns (queue, incoming, showing) Paths and mkdirs all three: <queue>/ (published *.png), <queue>/.incoming/ (webapp mid-conversion temp files), <queue>/.showing/ (player-claimed, being displayed). Both work subdirs are DOTFILES so a plain glob('*.png') on <queue>/ excludes them -- the webapp's queue-length count must likewise count only <queue>/*.png (use vsmp.list_queue(queue_dir), which returns them sorted = FIFO by lexical name, so uploads MUST use sortable monotonic-timestamp filenames per design doc section 3, e.g. <ms>_<counter>_<rand>.png). Player claims via claim_next_image() = os.rename oldest published *.png into .showing/ (atomic, tolerates the FileNotFoundError race). dispose_shown_image() deletes by default, or if VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR is set moves to the archive and prunes to the most-recent VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX (default 50) by sorted name. sweep_showing() deletes leftover .showing/ files at startup (mirrors clean_frame_dir).

State: 'images_shown' added to new_state() (seeds 0), surfaced in summarize_state() and printed by cmd_status ('images shown N'); load_state() setdefault keeps older state files valid.

PLAY-LOOP SHAPE DECISION: play_movie() loops `while state['frame'] < total or list_queue(queue_dir):`. At the TOP of each tick claim_next_image() runs BEFORE render_one_frame. On an image tick it prepare_for_panel + display_on_e_ink + dispose + increment images_shown + advance next_deadline (same behind-schedule re-anchoring as the movie path) + save_state + log 'image=<name> images_shown=N next=...' + watchdog_ping + sleep_until + continue -- WITHOUT advancing state['frame'] or touching any movie frame field, so the film resumes exactly where it paused. Because the while-condition also keys on a non-empty queue, uploads keep displaying AFTER the film's last frame within a running process. ONE DEVIATION a later feature should know about: the existing 'finished movie, nothing to do' early-return in cmd_play() was left UNCHANGED per the FEAT-001 option. Consequence: if the player STARTS with an already-finished movie (cold start, state.finished=True) and --restart is not given, cmd_play returns 0 before play_movie is ever entered, so a queue is NOT serviced in that cold-start-finished case. Queue servicing after end-of-movie only happens within a process that was already playing. If FEAT-002/UX needs uploads to display even from a cold-finished start, that early-return in cmd_play is the single place to relax (e.g. skip the early return when list_queue(queue_dir) is non-empty).
